mentions.name: Babel Nexus
mentions.description: Babel Nexus is a web app that offers free ebook applications, including a "Beyond the Public Domain" section that recently gained several new free ebook apps. After billing issues with its previous hosting, it is being rebuilt on the author's home computer using PowerShell and VS Code, with plans to host it long-term on Railway; the currently live site is a placeholder.
mentions.source_excerpt: I continue working on my side project Babel Nexus.
mentions.author: NishanStepak

mentions.name: Babel Nexus
mentions.description: This app is a discovery system for the public domain, organizing 773 primary works (books, papers, and reports) into a three-floor knowledge graph of 52 hexagonal galleries across science, literature, and wisdom. It includes an AI Oracle powered by Google Gemini that answers free-form questions about the archive, and has added public domain audiobooks to some titles, with plans to expand into films, comics, and other public domain media.
mentions.source_excerpt: I continue working on Babel Nexus https://babelnexus.com Explore classic books and big ideas in a whole new way — a discovery system for the public domain. A three-floor knowledge graph: 21 science hexagonal galleries on Level I, 23 literature hexagonal galleries on Level II, and 8 wisdom hexagonal galleries on Level III — 52 hexagonal galleries holding 773 primary works (books, papers, and reports, every one in the public domain), plus an AI Oracle (powered by Google Gemini) that answers free-form questions about the Archive.
mentions.author: NishanStepak

mentions.name: Babel Nexus
mentions.description: Babel Nexus is a proof-of-concept website that uses hexagonal gallery layouts to hold collections of books and media, inspired by the layout in Jorge Luis Borges' story The Library of Babel, and explores hexagonal architecture inside websites.
mentions.source_excerpt: I have been working on Babel Nexus https://babelnexus.com  It is a proof of concept for a site that uses hexagonal galleries.  I wanted to show that it was possible to use the layout in the story from The Library of Babel by Jorge Luis Borges to put other things in it like collections of books and media.  It is partially about hexagonal architecture inside websites.
mentions.author: NishanStepak

mentions.name: Babel Nexus
mentions.description: A public domain ebook repository that organizes knowledge using core collection theory. Inspired by the hexagonal galleries in Borges' The Library of Babel, it places content into hexagonal galleries and uses a spiral staircase concept to group kinds of knowledge across levels, mapping the hexagons to knowledge graphs with nodes and edges. It also includes reading trails and cortex maps, and is framed as an experimental art project mixing public domain books with philosophizing.
mentions.source_excerpt: I am playing around with creating a public domain repository for ebooks.  https://babelnexus.com  There are a few differences.
